rounds.text: Supreme Petrochem Ltd is demonstrating powerful, accelerating fundamental momentum characterized by a 40% trailing-twelve-month compounded profit growth [E21] and a massive net profit increase of 191% YoY [E65], supported by a recent quarterly operating margin of 20% compared to 8% in the year-ago quarter [E31]. This operational excellence translates to robust capital efficiency, featuring a strong ROCE of 18.8% [E12] and historical median ROEs of 24% over ten years [E26] and 23% over five years [E27], comfortably outperforming sector benchmarks [E10]. The company is conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.05x [E38] and borrowings reduced to Rs 126 Cr [E39], while a dramatic -87.3% drop in Capital Work in Progress to Rs 74 Cr indicates that major capex is largely completed and new capacity is primed to come online [E40]. Institutional conviction is clearly building behind these operational tailwinds, evidenced by increases in both foreign and domestic institutional shareholdings since September 2023 [E42, E43] alongside a positive money flow signal [E44] and a supportive chemical sector tailwind score [E69, E71]. Conceded: [E45] and [E46] show a DCF-based intrinsic value of Rs 284 yielding a negative margin of safety, and [E61] flags poor five-year sales growth of 10.9%.

Supreme Petrochem Ltd carries an egregious valuation and a severe underlying growth stagnation that the current market price of ₹704 fails to justify [E1, E2, E45]. The stock trades at a premium P/E of 27x to 28.41x and a P/B of 5.59x to 5.81x, both comfortably above sector benchmarks of 22.59x and 1.87x respectively [E1, E2, E6, E7]. More concerningly, a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of ₹284 per share, resulting in a staggering margin of safety deficiency of -147.9% [E45, E46]. This rich pricing is detached from reality when looking at top-line performance: compounded sales growth has completely stalled at 0% over the last 3 years and contracted by -3% over the trailing twelve months [E16, E17]. Profitability history paints an equally volatile picture with 5-year and 3-year compounded profit growth resting at -7% and -12% respectively, alongside an inconsistent yearly operating-margin trend [E19, E20, E32]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.05x, robust ROCE of 18.41%, and a recent spike in quarterly operating margins to 20% in June 2026 [E10, E31, E38]. Yet, with a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -83.0% and a reverse DCF implying that today's price already demands a demanding 12.6% earnings growth rate, the risk-reward skew heavily penalizes new buyers [E47, E53].

Conceded: the discounted cash flow model puts intrinsic value at ₹284 and the reverse DCF implies a 12.6% earnings growth rate [E45, E47]. However, the bear relies on stale backward-looking metrics while ignoring an active corporate turnaround and surging profitability [E70]. Compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has surged by 40%, supported by a massive net profit increase of 191% year-over-year [E21, E65]. Operating margins tell the same story of operational excellence, jumping to 20% in June 2026 compared to just 8% in the same quarter a year ago [E31]. This is reinforced by a robust sector tailwind score of +0.76 and strong institutional accumulation, with foreign and domestic institutional holdings both rising since September 2023 [E42, E43, E71]. Furthermore, capital expenditure is nearing fruition as construction work-in-progress dropped 87.3% to ₹74 Cr, signaling that new capacity is coming online right as momentum accelerates [E40].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth reached 40% alongside a 191% year-over-year net profit spike and a June 2026 quarterly operating margin of 20% [E21, E31, E65]. However, the bull's dismissal of the valuation risk is dangerously shortsighted because the intrinsic valuation gap is extreme, with a DCF intrinsic value of ₹284 against a market price of ₹704, creating a massive -147.9% margin of safety [E45, E46]. The bull highlights rising institutional holding, but this speculative accumulation ignores severe underlying top-line stagnation, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 0% and a trailing twelve-month sales contraction of -3% [E16, E17, E42, E43]. Conceded: capital expenditure is nearing fruition as construction work-in-progress dropped 87.3% to ₹74 Cr [E40]. Yet this newly completed capacity arrives into a highly cyclical business model that has delivered an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trend over the last three periods, alongside a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -83.0% [E32, E33, E53, E58]. Finally, the reverse DCF proves that the current share price already aggressively prices in 12.6% earnings growth—far higher than the baseline 0.0% expectation—meaning the market has already fully capitalized the bull's turnaround narrative long before it translates to sustainable, long-term top-line expansion [E47].
